# Variation: ChartType=Bar Chart, Library=seaborn
import pandas as pd
import seaborn as sns
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt

# -------------------------------------------------
# Data: Male education levels in Spain for 2005, 2010 & 2015
# Minor tweaks:
#   • Added a new category "Continuing Ed"
#   • Introduced a third year (2015) to show a continued trend
#   • Adjusted counts slightly while preserving the original story
# -------------------------------------------------
education_levels = [
    "Primary", "Secondary", "Associate",
    "Tertiary", "Post‑grad", "Doctorate",
    "Vocational", "Adult Education", "Continuing Ed"
]

# Counts are in thousands
counts_2005 = [21, 16, 15, 22, 12, 8, 10, 5, 4]   # Primary +1, new category added
counts_2010 = [23, 18, 16, 25, 13, 9, 12, 6, 5]   # Primary +1, new category added
counts_2015 = [24, 19, 17, 26, 14,10, 13, 7, 6]   # Continued growth

# Build long‑form DataFrame suitable for a grouped bar chart
rows = []
for level, cnt in zip(education_levels, counts_2005):
    rows.append({"Education Level": level, "Year": "2005", "Count (k)": cnt})
for level, cnt in zip(education_levels, counts_2010):
    rows.append({"Education Level": level, "Year": "2010", "Count (k)": cnt})
for level, cnt in zip(education_levels, counts_2015):
    rows.append({"Education Level": level, "Year": "2015", "Count (k)": cnt})

df = pd.DataFrame(rows)

# -------------------------------------------------
# Plot – Grouped Bar Chart using Seaborn
# -------------------------------------------------
sns.set_style("whitegrid")
palette = sns.color_palette("Set2")  # A soft, aesthetically pleasing palette

g = sns.catplot(
    data=df,
    x="Education Level",
    y="Count (k)",
    hue="Year",
    kind="bar",
    height=6,
    aspect=1.5,
    palette=palette,
    legend_out=False
)

# Tidy up the axes and title
g.set_axis_labels("Education Level", "Number of Males (thousands)")
g.fig.suptitle("Male Education Attainment in Spain (2005 vs 2010 vs 2015)", fontsize=14, y=1.02)
g.set_xticklabels(rotation=45, ha="right")
g._legend.set_title("Year")
g._legend.set_bbox_to_anchor((1.02, 0.5))
g._legend.set_frame_on(True)

# Adjust layout and save
plt.tight_layout()
g.fig.savefig("male_education_spain_bar.png", dpi=300, bbox_inches="tight")

# Variation: ChartType=Bar Chart, Library=plotly
import pandas as pd
import plotly.express as px

# Updated data – still focuses on Niger’s trade with developing economies in the region
years = ['1969', '1970', '1971', '1972', '1973', '1974', '1975']
exports = [27, 33, 34, 34, 33, 35, 36]   # Merchandise exports (%)
imports = [13, 13, 12, 14, 15, 19, 20]   # Merchandise imports (%)

# Build a tidy DataFrame suitable for Plotly
df = pd.DataFrame({
    'Year': years * 2,
    'Metric': ['Exports'] * len(years) + ['Imports'] * len(years),
    'Share (%)': exports + imports
})

# Create a grouped vertical bar chart
fig = px.bar(
    df,
    x='Year',
    y='Share (%)',
    color='Metric',
    barmode='group',
    color_discrete_sequence=['#4C78A8', '#F58518'],  # a calm, contrasting palette
    title='Niger – Merchandise Trade with Developing Economies (1969‑1975)',
    labels={'Share (%)': 'Trade share within region (%)'}
)

# Refine layout for clarity
fig.update_layout(
    xaxis_title='Year',
    yaxis_title='Share of Trade (%)',
    legend_title_text='',
    legend=dict(
        orientation='h',
        yanchor='bottom',
        y=1.02,
        xanchor='right',
        x=1
    ),
    margin=dict(l=60, r=20, t=80, b=60)
)

# Save the figure to a static PNG file (requires the "kaleido" package)
fig.write_image("niger_trade_bar.png")

    'Italy': [10.0, 10.5, 9.5, 8.5],

    'Iran': [5.5, 5.0, 4.5, 4.0],
    'Indonesia': [21.0, 20.5, 22.0, 23.0]
}

# Colors
colors = ['#8B5F3B', '#CD5B6C', '#FFBF77', '#FF9933']

# Plotting
fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(10, 6))

# Bar width
bar_width = 0.2

# Positions for the bars
positions = np.arange(len(countries))

# Create bars for each year
for i, year in enumerate(years):
    emissions_year = [emissions[country][i] for country in countries]
    ax.barh(positions + i * bar_width, emissions_year, bar_width, label=str(year), color=colors[i])

# Adding labels and title
ax.set_xlabel('Emissions (in percent)')
ax.set_ylabel('Country')
ax.set_title('CO2 emissions from gaseous fuel consumption')
ax.set_yticks(positions + bar_width * 1.5)
ax.set_yticklabels(countries)

# Show plot
plt.tight_layout()

import pandas as pd

import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import numpy as np

# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
# 1.  Original enrollment data (male primary net enrollment, % points)
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
countries = [
    "Latin America", "South Korea", "Pakistan", "Syria", "Vietnam",
    "Indonesia", "Thailand", "Philippines", "Cambodia", "Myanmar",
    "Laos", "Bangladesh", "Sri Lanka", "India", "Ethiopia",
    "Kenya", "Nigeria", "Ghana", "Japan", "Morocco", "Egypt",
    "Jordan"          # added country for a richer dataset
]

enrollment_2024 = [
    108, 99, 99, 97, 100,
    99, 96, 94, 88, 89,
    86, 84, 90, 93, 82,
    82, 85, 80, 90, 78, 81,
    92               # Jordan 2024
]

enrollment_2025 = [
    110, 101, 100, 99, 102,
    101, 98, 95, 90, 90,
    88, 85, 92, 95, 84,
    84, 87, 82, 92, 80, 83,
    94               # Jordan 2025 (slight rise)
]

enrollment_2026 = [
    113, 103, 102, 100, 105,
    104, 100, 97, 93, 92,
    91, 88, 95, 97, 87,
    86, 90, 85, 95, 82, 86,
    96               # Jordan 2026 (steady increase)
]

# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
# 2. Build the dataframe
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
df_raw = pd.DataFrame({
    "Country": countries,
    "2024": enrollment_2024,
    "2025": enrollment_2025,
    "2026": enrollment_2026
}).set_index("Country")

# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
# 3. Map each country to a broader region (now four regions)
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
region_map = {
    # Latin America
    "Latin America": "Latin America",
    # Asia
    "South Korea": "Asia", "Pakistan": "Asia", "Vietnam": "Asia",
    "Indonesia": "Asia", "Thailand": "Asia", "Philippines": "Asia",
    "Cambodia": "Asia", "Myanmar": "Asia", "Laos": "Asia",

    "Japan": "Asia",
    # Africa
    "Ethiopia": "Africa", "Kenya": "Africa", "Nigeria": "Africa",
    "Ghana": "Africa", "Morocco": "Africa", "Egypt": "Africa",
    # Middle East (new region)
    "Syria": "Middle East", "Jordan": "Middle East"
}
df_raw["Region"] = df_raw.index.map(region_map)

# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
# 4. Aggregate enrollment totals per region for each year
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
region_totals = df_raw.groupby("Region")[["2024", "2025", "2026"]].sum()

# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
# 5. Create a modest 2027 projection (5 % drop from 2026 totals)
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
region_totals["2027"] = (region_totals["2026"] * 0.95).round().astype(int)

region_totals = region_totals[["2024", "2025", "2026", "2027"]]

# ----------------------------------------------------------------------

palette = sns.color_palette("Set2")   # fresh pastel palette different from original

plt.figure(figsize=(10, 6))
barplot = sns.barplot(data=df_plot,

                      y="Enrollment",

                      palette=palette,
                      edgecolor="black")

# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
# 8. Save the figure
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------

})

import seaborn as sns
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt

# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
# Extended dataset (1992‑2050) – Renewable electricity share (% of total)
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------

    (1992, 1.7), (1993, 1.8), (1994, 1.9), (1995, 2.1), (1996, 2.2),
    (1997, 2.3), (1998, 2.5), (1999, 2.7), (2000, 3.0), (2001, 3.1),

    (2007, 4.0), (2008, 4.2), (2009, 4.4), (2010, 4.5), (2011, 4.7),
    (2012, 5.0), (2013, 5.2), (2014, 5.7), (2015, 5.9), (2016, 6.1),
    (2017, 6.4), (2018, 6.6), (2019, 6.9), (2020, 7.3), (2021, 7.5),
    (2022, 7.8), (2023, 8.0), (2024, 8.2), (2025, 8.5), (2026, 8.7),
    (2027, 8.9), (2028, 9.0), (2029, 9.2), (2030, 9.5), (2031, 9.6),
    (2032, 9.8), (2033, 10.0), (2034, 10.2), (2035, 10.5),
    (2036, 10.8), (2037, 11.0), (2038, 11.2), (2039, 11.4), (2040, 11.6),
    (2041, 11.9), (2042, 12.1), (2043, 12.3), (2044, 12.5), (2045, 12.8),
    (2046, 13.0), (2047, 13.2), (2048, 13.5), (2049, 13.8), (2050, 14.1)
]
df = pd.DataFrame(raw_data, columns=['Year', 'ActualShare'])

# Soft policy targets: +5 %, +10 %, +15 %
df['Target5']  = (df['ActualShare'] * 1.05).round(2)
df['Target10'] = (df['ActualShare'] * 1.10).round(2)
df['Target15'] = (df['ActualShare'] * 1.15).round(2)

# Assign decade labels (now including 2050s)
def decade_label(y):
    if y < 2000:
        return '1990s'
    elif y < 2010:
        return '2000s'
    elif y < 2020:
        return '2010s'
    elif y < 2030:
        return '2020s'
    elif y < 2040:
        return '2030s'
    elif y < 2050:
        return '2040s'
    else:
        return '2050s'

df['Decade'] = df['Year'].apply(decade_label)

# Compute decadal averages for each scenario
agg = (
    df.groupby('Decade')
      .agg(
          ActualAvg=('ActualShare', 'mean'),
          Target5Avg=('Target5', 'mean'),
          Target10Avg=('Target10', 'mean'),
          Target15Avg=('Target15', 'mean')
      )
      .reset_index()
      .sort_values('Decade')
)

# Reshape for Seaborn (long format)
agg_long = pd.melt(
    agg,
    id_vars='Decade',
    value_vars=['ActualAvg', 'Target5Avg', 'Target10Avg', 'Target15Avg'],
    var_name='Scenario',
    value_name='AverageShare'
)

# Make scenario names pretty
scenario_map = {
    'ActualAvg': 'Actual',
    'Target5Avg': 'Target (+5%)',
    'Target10Avg': 'Target (+10%)',
    'Target15Avg': 'Target (+15%)'
}
agg_long['Scenario'] = agg_long['Scenario'].map(scenario_map)

# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
# Plot grouped bar chart with Seaborn
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
sns.set_style('whitegrid')
palette = sns.color_palette('colorblind', n_colors=4)

plt.figure(figsize=(10, 6))
barplot = sns.barplot(
    data=agg_long,
    x='Decade',
    y='AverageShare',
    hue='Scenario',
    palette=palette,
    edgecolor='black'
)

# Title and axis labels
barplot.set_title('Decadal Average Renewable Electricity Share\n(Actual vs. Soft Targets)', pad=15)
barplot.set_xlabel('Decade')
barplot.set_ylabel('Average Share (%)')

# Adjust legend
plt.legend(title='Scenario', loc='upper left', bbox_to_anchor=(1, 1))

# Tight layout and save
plt.tight_layout()
plt.savefig('renewables_bar_seaborn.png', dpi=300, bbox_inches='tight')
plt.close()

import pandas as pd
import seaborn as sns
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt

# Expanded data (Employment‑to‑population ratio % for ages 15‑24)
years = list(range(2005, 2016))  # 2005‑2015 inclusive
female_rates = [45, 46, 47, 44, 48, 49, 50, 51, 50, 52, 53]  # modest upward trend
male_rates   = [51, 53, 52, 47, 55, 54, 56, 55, 57, 58, 59]

df = pd.DataFrame({
    "Year": years * 2,
    "Gender": ["Female"] * len(years) + ["Male"] * len(years),
    "EmploymentRate": female_rates + male_rates
})

# Treat Year as categorical to keep bars evenly spaced
df["Year"] = df["Year"].astype(str)

sns.set_style("whitegrid")
plt.figure(figsize=(10, 6))

# A soft, distinct palette different from the original
palette = {"Female": "#ff9999",  # light red
           "Male":   "#66b3ff"}  # light blue

sns.barplot(
    data=df,
    x="Year",
    y="EmploymentRate",
    hue="Gender",
    palette=palette,
    ci=None  # no confidence interval shading
)

plt.title("Employment‑to‑Population Ratio (15‑24 yr) – Ireland",
          fontsize=14, pad=15)
plt.xlabel("Year", fontsize=12)
plt.ylabel("Employment Ratio (%)", fontsize=12)

# Legend placed outside the plot area
plt.legend(title="", loc='upper left', bbox_to_anchor=(1, 1))

plt.tight_layout()
plt.savefig("employment_bar_chart.png", dpi=300, bbox_inches='tight')
plt.close()

# ------------------------------------------------------------------

# ------------------------------------------------------------------
years = list(range(1985, 1997))  # 1985‑1996 (12 years)

# Slightly adjusted percentages (original values +1% for illustration)
debt_pct = [26, 30, 31, 24, 24, 27, 26, 28, 25, 29, 27, 27]       # External Debt (% of exports)
repayment_pct = [9, 10, 8, 11, 10, 12, 11, 13, 12, 14, 13, 13]   # IMF Repayment (% of exports)

# Build a tidy DataFrame (optional, useful for inspection)
df = pd.DataFrame({
    "Year": years,
    "External Debt": debt_pct,
    "IMF Repayment": repayment_pct
})

# ------------------------------------------------------------------
# Plotting a grouped bar chart with Plotly
# ------------------------------------------------------------------
fig = go.Figure(data=[
    go.Bar(
        name="External Debt",
        x=df["Year"],
        y=df["External Debt"],
        marker_color="rgb(31, 119, 180)"          # muted blue from Plotly's palette
    ),
    go.Bar(
        name="IMF Repayment",
        x=df["Year"],
        y=df["IMF Repayment"],
        marker_color="rgb(255, 127, 14)"          # warm orange from Plotly's palette
    )
])

fig.update_layout(
    title="External Debt vs. IMF Repayments (% of Exports) by Year",
    xaxis_title="Year",
    yaxis_title="Percentage of Exports (%)",
    legend_title_text="Metric",
    barmode="group",
    template="simple_white",
    xaxis=dict(tickmode="linear")  # ensure every year is shown
)

# Save the figure as a PNG image (requires the 'kaleido' package)
fig.write_image("tunisia_debt_imf_bar.png", width=800, height=500, scale=2)

# Variation: ChartType=Bar Chart, Library=seaborn
import pandas as pd
import seaborn as sns
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt

# ------------------------------------------------------------------
# Credit‑Information Index per region for three consecutive years
# ------------------------------------------------------------------
regions = [
    "Europe (developing)",
    "Cyprus",
    "Singapore",
    "Other",
    "Australia",
    "New Zealand"
]
years = ["2021", "2022", "2023"]

# Minor adjustments: added New Zealand and tweaked a few values
values = {
    "2021": [5.5, 3.0, 7.0, 1.5, 2.5, 2.8],
    "2022": [6.5, 4.0, 7.0, 2.0, 3.0, 3.2],
    "2023": [6.6, 6.2, 7.0, 1.8, 3.5, 3.7],
}

# Build a tidy DataFrame for seaborn
records = {"Region": [], "Year": [], "Index": []}
for yr in years:
    for reg, val in zip(regions, values[yr]):
        records["Region"].append(reg)
        records["Year"].append(yr)
        records["Index"].append(val)

df = pd.DataFrame(records)

# --------------------------------------------------------------
# Plot: grouped bar chart (Region on x‑axis, Index on y‑axis)
# --------------------------------------------------------------
sns.set_style("whitegrid")
palette = sns.color_palette("viridis", n_colors=len(years))

plt.figure(figsize=(10, 6))
sns.barplot(
    data=df,
    x="Region",
    y="Index",
    hue="Year",
    palette=palette,
    edgecolor="black"
)

plt.title("Credit‑Information Index by Region (2021‑2023)",
          fontsize=14, weight="bold")
plt.xlabel("Region", fontsize=12)
plt.ylabel("Index", fontsize=12)

# Ensure region labels are readable
plt.xticks(rotation=30, ha="right")

# Position legend without covering data
plt.legend(title="Year", loc="upper right")

plt.tight_layout()
plt.savefig("bar_chart.png", dpi=300)
plt.close()

    records.append({"IncomeBracket": bracket, "Gender": "Female", "Rate": f})

# Variation: ChartType=Bar, Library=Matplotlib

import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import numpy as np

# Data
years = [2005, 2006, 2008, 2009, 2010]
east_asia = [94, 94, 94, 95, 95]
bangladesh = [91, 91, 91, 92, 93]
iceland = [99, 99, 99, 99, 99]
norway = [99, 99, 99, 99, 99]

# Width of the bars
bar_width = 0.2

# Positions of the bars on the x-axis
r1 = np.arange(len(years))
r2 = [x + bar_width for x in r1]
r3 = [x + bar_width for x in r2]
r4 = [x + bar_width for x in r3]

# Create the figure and axis
fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(12, 8))

# Plot the bars
ax.barh(r1, east_asia, color='blue', edgecolor='white', height=bar_width, label='East Asia (developing only)')
ax.barh(r2, bangladesh, color='magenta', edgecolor='white', height=bar_width, label='Bangladesh')
ax.barh(r3, iceland, color='olive', edgecolor='white', height=bar_width, label='Iceland')
ax.barh(r4, norway, color='salmon', edgecolor='white', height=bar_width, label='Norway')

# Add labels, title, and custom x-axis tick labels
ax.set_xlabel('Net enrolment rate(%)')
ax.set_title('Net enrolment rate of males in primary schools')
ax.set_yticks([r + 1.5 * bar_width for r in range(len(years))])

# Extended data (still reflecting a gradual downward trend)

                  1.05, 1.00]  # continued decline

    "Year": years,
    "Migrant_Stocks_Percent": stocks_percent
})

plt.figure(figsize=(10, 6))
sns.barplot(
    x="Year",
    y="Migrant_Stocks_Percent",
    data=df,
    palette=palette,
    edgecolor="black"
)

}

# Create the figure and axis

# Plot bars

# Add labels, title, and legend

ax.set_yticklabels(categories)

import pandas as pd
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt

# --------------------------------------------------------------
# Data: IMF credit disbursements (actual) 1990‑2024 (minor tweaks)
# --------------------------------------------------------------
years = list(range(1990, 2025))  # 1990‑2024 inclusive

# Base values (original series + a modest 2024 forecast)
base_credit = [
    1.22, 1.18, 1.12, 1.07, 1.02, 0.99, 0.94, 0.89, 0.85, 0.78,
    0.73, 0.68, 0.63, 0.60, 0.57, 0.54, 0.51, 0.48, 0.45, 0.42,
    0.40, 0.38, 0.36, 0.34, 0.32, 0.30, 0.28, 0.27, 0.26, 0.25,
    0.24, 0.23, 0.22,   # 2022 (slightly lower than 2021)
    0.20,               # 2023 (continuing the downward trend)
    0.18                # 2024 forecast (small further decline)
]

# Apply alternating factor (1.015 for even index, 0.985 for odd) and a tiny upward shift
credit_actual = [
    round(val * (1.015 if i % 2 == 0 else 0.985) + 0.05 + 0.03 + 0.01, 3)
    for i, val in enumerate(base_credit)
]

# Assemble DataFrame
df = pd.DataFrame({
    "Year": years,
    "IMF Disbursement (US$ Bn)": credit_actual
})

# Policy phase classification (used for stacked bars)
def policy_phase(y):
    return "Pre‑2008" if y < 2008 else "Post‑2008"

df["Policy Phase"] = df["Year"].apply(policy_phase)

# Columns for stacking
df["Pre‑2008"] = df.apply(
    lambda r: r["IMF Disbursement (US$ Bn)"] if r["Policy Phase"] == "Pre‑2008" else 0,
    axis=1
)
df["Post‑2008"] = df.apply(
    lambda r: r["IMF Disbursement (US$ Bn)"] if r["Policy Phase"] == "Post‑2008" else 0,
    axis=1
)

# --------------------------------------------------------------
# Plot: Stacked Bar Chart using Matplotlib
# --------------------------------------------------------------
# Choose a pastel colour scheme
pre_color = "#a6cee3"   # Pastel blue
post_color = "#1f78b4"  # Slightly deeper blue for contrast

fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(12, 6))

# Pre‑2008 segment
ax.bar(df["Year"], df["Pre‑2008"], label="Pre‑2008", color=pre_color)

# Post‑2008 segment stacked on top
ax.bar(df["Year"], df["Post‑2008"], bottom=df["Pre‑2008"],
       label="Post‑2008", color=post_color)

# Layout adjustments
ax.set_title(
    "IMF Credit Disbursements (1990‑2024) – Stacked by Policy Phase",
    fontsize=14,
    pad=15
)
ax.set_xlabel("Year")
ax.set_ylabel("Disbursement (US$ Billion)")

# Show every second year to keep x‑axis readable
ax.set_xticks(df["Year"][::2])
ax.tick_params(axis='x', rotation=45)

ax.legend(title="Policy Phase", loc="upper left")
ax.grid(axis='y', linestyle='--', alpha=0.6)

plt.tight_layout()
fig.savefig("imf_credit_bar.png", dpi=300)

# ---- Data preparation ----
# Years 2013‑2035 (23 years) with slight deterministic deviations from the historical mean (6.8)
years = list(range(2013, 2036))

# Minor extensions to the original deviations (kept close to the original series)
deviation = [
    -0.130, -0.108, 0.215, -0.460, -0.118,
    -0.078, 0.218, -0.128, 0.560, 0.208,
    0.053, 0.120, -0.030, 0.075, 0.090,
    -0.050, 0.100, 0.020, -0.040, 0.060,
    0.070, -0.020, 0.030  # new values for 2032‑2034
]

mean_index = 6.8
# Compute the yearly index values
index_value = [round(mean_index + d, 3) for d in deviation]

# Categorical label to colour‑code bars (above or below the long‑term mean)
trend = ["Above" if val >= mean_index else "Below" for val in index_value]

# Assemble the DataFrame
df = pd.DataFrame({
    "Year": [str(y) for y in years],
    "IndexValue": index_value,
    "Trend": trend
})

# ---- Bar Chart (Seaborn) ----
sns.set_style("whitegrid")

# Custom palette: green for 'Above', red for 'Below'
palette = {"Above": "#2ca02c", "Below": "#d62728"}

    x="Year",
    y="IndexValue",
    hue="Trend",
    palette=palette,
    dodge=False
)

    [75, 78, 77, 74, 78, 80, 73],   # 2025 (steady improvement)
]

# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
# Transform to tidy DataFrame

    [
        {"Year": yr, "Region": reg, "Coverage": cov}
        for yr, row in zip(years, coverage_by_year)
        for reg, cov in zip(regions, row)
    ]
)

    1.85                               # Ghana (new entry)
]

modest_decrease = [round(v - 0.02, 3) for v in baseline]      # slightly lower than baseline

    "Modest Increase": modest_increase,
    "Modest Decrease": modest_decrease,

})

import pandas as pd
import seaborn as sns
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt

# -------------------------------------------------
# Updated Data: Net resource balances (million USD)
# Added France and an intermediate 1974 projection.
# Minor numeric tweaks (≈+2% overall) keep story consistent.
# -------------------------------------------------
countries = ["Chile", "Canada", "Brazil", "India", "Japan", "Germany", "France"]
years = [1965, 1971, 1974, 1977]  # include projected 1974 for richer bar groups

# Base surplus values (1965, 1971) – increased by ~2%
surplus_data = {
    "Chile":   [int(round(66 * 1.02)), int(round(72 * 1.02))],
    "Canada":  [int(round(805 * 1.02)), int(round(895 * 1.02))],
    "Brazil":  [int(round(317 * 1.02)), int(round(347 * 1.02))],
    "India":   [int(round(397 * 1.02)), int(round(437 * 1.02))],
    "Japan":   [int(round(373 * 1.02)), int(round(411 * 1.02))],
    "Germany": [int(round(582 * 1.02)), int(round(642 * 1.02))],
    "France":  [int(round(510 * 1.02)), int(round(560 * 1.02))],
}

# Base deficit values (1965, 1971) – increased by ~2%
deficit_data = {
    "Chile":   [int(round(28 * 1.02)), int(round(30 * 1.02))],
    "Canada":  [int(round(158 * 1.02)), int(round(174 * 1.02))],
    "Brazil":  [int(round(121 * 1.02)), int(round(133 * 1.02))],
    "India":   [int(round(197 * 1.02)), int(round(217 * 1.02))],
    "Japan":   [int(round(68 * 1.02)), int(round(76 * 1.02))],
    "Germany": [int(round(135 * 1.02)), int(round(149 * 1.02))],
    "France":  [int(round( ninety * 1.02)) for ninety in [92]],  # placeholder, will be overridden below
}

# Manually set France deficit (1965, 1971) to keep pattern consistent
deficit_data["France"] = [int(round(92 * 1.02)), int(round(102 * 1.02))]

def project(value, years_ahead):
    """Apply a 5 % growth per 3‑year step, plus an extra 1 % on the final 1977 step."""
    for i in range(years_ahead // 3):
        value = round(value * 1.05)
    if years_ahead == 12:  # 1977 is 12 years after 1965 → three steps, last step gets +1 %
        value = round(value * 1.01)
    return int(value)

def get_surplus(country, year):
    if year == 1965:
        return surplus_data[country][0]
    if year == 1971:
        return surplus_data[country][1]
    if year == 1974:
        return project(surplus_data[country][1], 3)       # one 5 % step from 1971
    if year == 1977:
        # two 5 % steps from 1971 then +1 %
        s = project(surplus_data[country][1], 6)
        return round(s * 1.01)
    raise ValueError

def get_deficit(country, year):
    if year == 1965:
        return deficit_data[country][0]
    if year == 1971:
        return deficit_data[country][1]
    if year == 1974:
        return project(deficit_data[country][1], 3)
    if year == 1977:
        d = project(deficit_data[country][1], 6)
        return round(d * 1.01)
    raise ValueError

# Assemble net balances into a tidy DataFrame
records = []
for country in countries:
    for year in years:
        net = get_surplus(country, year) - get_deficit(country, year)
        records.append({"Country": country, "Year": str(year), "NetBalance": net})

df = pd.DataFrame.from_records(records)

# -------------------------------------------------
# Bar chart with seaborn (grouped by Country, hue=Year)
# -------------------------------------------------

palette = sns.color_palette("Set2")  # fresh, pastel palette distinct from original

    aspect=1.5,

)

)

# Adjust legend position
g._legend.set_title("Year")
g._legend.set_bbox_to_anchor((1.02, 1))
g._legend.set_frame_on(True)

plt.tight_layout()
g.fig.savefig("resource_balance_bar.png", dpi=300, bbox_inches="tight")
plt.close(g.fig)

import matplotlib.pyplot as plt

# ---- Data definition (minor extensions) ----
countries = [
    "Indonesia",
    "Mauritius",
    "Norway",
    "Sweden",
    "Finland",
    "Canada",
    "Australia",
]

regions = {
    "Indonesia": "Asia",
    "Mauritius": "Africa",
    "Norway": "Europe",
    "Sweden": "Europe",
    "Finland": "Europe",
    "Canada": "North America",
    "Australia": "Oceania",
}

years = list(range(2007, 2018))  # 2007‑2017 inclusive

# Updated participation percentages (added 2017 values, slight tweaks)
base_values = {
    "Indonesia": [50, 51, 51, 51, 52, 53, 54, 55, 56, 57, 58],
    "Mauritius": [44, 45, 46, 47, 47, 48, 49, 50, 51, 52, 53],
    "Norway":    [76, 77, 76, 75, 75, 74, 73, 73, 72, 71, 70],
    "Sweden":    [78, 79, 80, 81, 81, 82, 83, 84, 85, 86, 87],
    "Finland":   [79, 80, 81, 82, 83, 84, 85, 86, 87, 88, 89],
    "Canada":    [81, 82, 82, 83, 84, 85, 86, 87, 88, 89, 90],
    "Australia": [80, 81, 81, 82, 83, 84, 85, 86, 87, 88, 89],
}

# Build long‑form DataFrame
records = []
for country in countries:
    for i, year in enumerate(years):
        records.append(
            {
                "Region": regions[country],
                "Country": country,
                "Year": year,
                "Participation": base_values[country][i],
            }
        )
df = pd.DataFrame.from_records(records)

# Aggregate to average participation per region across all years
avg_by_region = (
    df.groupby("Region")["Participation"]
    .mean()
    .reset_index()
    .rename(columns={"Participation": "AvgParticipation"})
)

# ---- Plotting (Bar Chart) ----
sns.set_style("whitegrid")
plt.figure(figsize=(10, 6))

barplot = sns.barplot(
    data=avg_by_region,
    x="Region",
    y="AvgParticipation",
    palette="Set2",               # aesthetically pleasing, different from original
    edgecolor="black",
)

# Titles and labels

)

# Variation: ChartType=Bar Chart, Library=seaborn
import pandas as pd
import seaborn as sns
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt

# Data: 15 observations per fiscal year (2009‑2023), values nudged +2 days
years = []
for yr in range(2009, 2024):
    years.extend([yr] * 15)

orig_processing_days = [
    # 2009
    26, 27, 29, 30, 31, 28, 32, 33, 25, 34, 35, 36, 28, 32, 34,
    # 2010
    32, 33, 34, 36, 35, 37, 38, 39, 31, 40, 41, 42, 33, 35, 37,
    # 2011
    35, 36, 38, 40, 37, 39, 41, 42, 34, 43, 44, 45, 36, 38, 40,
    # 2012
    40, 41, 42, 44, 43, 45, 46, 47, 39, 48, 49, 50, 41, 43, 45,
    # 2013
    42, 43, 44, 45, 46, 47, 48, 49, 41, 50, 51, 52, 44, 46, 48,
    # 2014
    46, 47, 48, 49, 50, 51, 52, 53, 45, 54, 55, 56, 48, 50, 52,
    # 2015
    53, 54, 55, 56, 57, 58, 59, 60, 52, 61, 62, 63, 55, 57, 59,
    # 2016
    58, 59, 60, 61, 62, 60, 63, 64, 57, 65, 66, 67, 59, 61, 63,
    # 2017
    66, 67, 68, 69, 70, 71, 72, 73, 74, 75, 76, 77, 68, 70, 72,
    # 2018
    70, 71, 72, 73, 74, 75, 76, 77, 78, 79, 80, 81, 72, 74, 76,
    # 2019
    73, 74, 75, 76, 77, 78, 79, 80, 81, 82, 83, 84, 75, 77, 79,
    # 2020
    78, 79, 80, 81, 82, 83, 84, 85, 86, 87, 88, 89, 80, 82, 84,
    # 2021
    90, 92, 93, 95, 96, 97, 98, 99, 101, 103, 104, 105, 107, 108, 110,
    # 2022
    112, 113, 115, 116, 117, 118, 119, 120, 122, 124, 126, 128, 130, 132, 134,
    # 2023
    136, 137, 138, 140, 141, 142, 144, 145, 147, 148, 150, 151, 152, 154, 156,
]

# Apply a gentle upward shift of +2 days to all observations
processing_days = [d + 2 for d in orig_processing_days]

df = pd.DataFrame({
    "FiscalYear": years,
    "ProcessingDays": processing_days,
})

# Aggregate: number of applications and average processing days per fiscal year
agg = (
    df.groupby("FiscalYear")
      .agg(Applications=("ProcessingDays", "size"),
           AvgDays=("ProcessingDays", "mean"))
      .reset_index()
)

# Create a readable label for the x‑axis
agg["FYLabel"] = agg["FiscalYear"].apply(lambda y: f"FY {y}")

# Plot – bar chart of average processing days
sns.set_style("whitegrid")
plt.figure(figsize=(12, 6))
bar_plot = sns.barplot(
    data=agg,
    x="FYLabel",
    y="AvgDays",
    palette="flare"
)

# Annotate each bar with the exact average value
for p in bar_plot.patches:
    height = p.get_height()
    bar_plot.annotate(f"{height:.1f}",
                      (p.get_x() + p.get_width() / 2., height),
                      ha='center', va='bottom',
                      fontsize=9,
                      xytext=(0, 4),
                      textcoords='offset points')

plt.title("Average License‑Processing Days by Fiscal Year (2009‑2023)", fontsize=14, pad=15)
plt.ylabel("Average Days", fontsize=12)
plt.xlabel("")
plt.xticks(rotation=45, ha='right')
plt.tight_layout()

# Save the figure
plt.savefig("license_processing_bar.png", dpi=300)
plt.close()

import pandas as pd
import plotly.express as px

# ---- Expanded data (9 grant values per country, new country Uganda) ----
data = {
    'Country': (
        ['Afghanistan'] * 9 +
        ['Lao PDR'] * 9 +
        ['Slovenia'] * 9 +
        ['Yemen'] * 9 +
        ['Kenya'] * 9 +
        ['Bangladesh'] * 9 +
        ['Nigeria'] * 9 +
        ['India'] * 9 +
        ['Pakistan'] * 9 +
        ['Ethiopia'] * 9 +          # existing new country
        ['Vietnam'] * 9 +           # existing new country
        ['Uganda'] * 9               # additional new country
    ),
    'Aid (USD millions)': (
        # Afghanistan (slightly higher values)
        [13, 9, 11, 8, 10, 12, 7, 10.5, 9.5] +
        # Lao PDR (minor tweaks)
        [2.1, 1.6, 3.1, 1.9, 2.3, 2.6, 2.0, 1.8, 2.2] +
        # Slovenia (small adjustments)
        [0.56, 0.61, 0.51, 0.66, 0.46, 0.71, 0.41, 0.60, 0.55] +
        # Yemen (updated)
        [4.1, 5.1, 3.6, 4.6, 6.1, 5.6, 3.9, 4.8, 5.0] +
        # Kenya (updated)
        [2.6, 3.1, 2.9, 3.3, 3.0, 3.6, 2.7, 3.2, 3.4] +
        # Bangladesh (updated)
        [3.1, 4.1, 3.6, 4.3, 3.9, 4.6, 3.3, 4.0, 4.2] +
        # Nigeria (updated)
        [1.1, 1.3, 1.0, 1.2, 0.9, 1.4, 0.8, 1.25, 1.15] +
        # India (updated)
        [2.1, 2.6, 2.3, 2.9, 2.4, 2.8, 2.0, 2.7, 2.5] +
        # Pakistan (updated)
        [1.6, 1.9, 2.1, 1.7, 2.3, 2.0, 2.2, 1.85, 2.05] +
        # Ethiopia (new data, similar magnitude)
        [2.4, 2.8, 2.5, 2.9, 3.0, 2.7, 2.3, 2.6, 2.9] +
        # Vietnam (new data, slightly higher)
        [3.0, 3.5, 3.2, 3.8, 4.0, 3.6, 3.1, 3.7, 3.9] +
        # Uganda (new data, modest values)
        [1.8, 2.1, 1.9, 2.3, 2.0, 2.2, 1.7, 2.0, 2.1]
    )
}

df = pd.DataFrame(data)

# ---- Summary statistics per country ----
summary = (
    df.groupby('Country')['Aid (USD millions)']
    .agg(Average_Aid='mean', Total_Aid='sum')
    .reset_index()
)

# Transform to long format for grouped bar chart
long_df = pd.melt(
    summary,
    id_vars='Country',
    value_vars=['Average_Aid', 'Total_Aid'],
    var_name='Metric',
    value_name='Value'
)

# ---- Bar Chart: Average vs Total Aid per Country ----
fig = px.bar(
    long_df,
    x='Country',
    y='Value',
    color='Metric',
    barmode='group',
    color_discrete_sequence=px.colors.qualitative.Pastel,
    title='Canadian Aid: Average vs. Total Grants per Country',
    labels={'Value': 'Aid (USD million)', 'Country': 'Country'}
)

# Fine‑tune layout
fig.update_layout(
    xaxis_tickangle=-45,
    legend_title_text='Metric',
    legend=dict(x=1.02, y=1, bordercolor='Gray', borderwidth=1),
    margin=dict(l=60, r=60, t=80, b=80),
    plot_bgcolor='rgba(0,0,0,0)'
)

# Save static PNG

                "Peri Urban", "Outer Rural", "Semi Urban",

        base = df[(df["Year"] == 1994) & (df["Category"] == cat)]
        if not base.empty:
            share = base["Share"].iloc[0] - 0.2  # small reduction
            extra_rows.append({"Year": yr, "Category": cat, "Share": round(share, 1)})

# 3. Introduce a new sub‑category "Coastal Urban" for years >=2000

for yr in df["Year"].unique():
    if yr >= 2000:
        coastal_urban_rows.append({
            "Year": yr,
            "Category": "Coastal Urban",
            "Share": 0.8 + (yr - 2000) * 0.02  # gradual increase
        })

# 4. Slightly bump shares for the most recent period (year >=2000)

    2050, 2100, 2200, 2100, 2300, 2520,

    1700, 1650, 1600, 1550, 1500, 1450,
    1460, 1480, 1500, 1520, 1550, 1580,
    1600, 1620
]

    13.6, 12.1, 12.5, 11.5, 17.0, 18.1,
    16.6, 15.5, 14.5, 13.5, 11.5, 10.5,
    9.8, 9.2, 8.7, 8.3, 7.9, 7.5,
    7.0, 6.8, 6.5, 6.3, 6.1, 5.9,
    5.6, 5.3
]

survivors = [round(c * r / 100) for c, r in zip(cohort_sizes, survival_rates)]

# --------------------------------------------------------------

df_wide = pd.DataFrame({
    "Year": years,
    "CohortSize": cohort_sizes,
    "Survivors": survivors
})

                       var_name="Metric",

    y="Count",
    color="Metric",
    barmode="group",

import seaborn as sns
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import pandas as pd
import numpy as np

# --------------------------------------------------------------
# Years (1996‑2015) – added 2015 as a new projection year
# --------------------------------------------------------------
years = [
    "1996", "1997", "1998", "1999", "2000", "2001", "2002",
    "2003", "2004", "2005", "2006", "2007", "2008", "2009",
    "2010", "2011", "2012", "2013", "2014", "2015"
]

# --------------------------------------------------------------
# Base trade volumes (export + import) for each year (bn £)
# Slightly increased each value by 0.02 bn £ to illustrate a minor tweak.
# --------------------------------------------------------------
base_trade = [
    0.792, 0.818, 0.828, 0.833, 0.868, 0.899, 0.929,
    0.965, 0.988, 1.025, 1.056, 1.085, 1.115, 1.145,
    1.177, 1.207, 1.231, 1.250, 1.280, 1.300   # 2015 projection
]

# --------------------------------------------------------------
# Scenarios: ±2 % variation around each base value
# --------------------------------------------------------------
scenarios = ["Low (-2 %)", "Base", "High (+2 %)"]

# Build a tidy DataFrame suitable for seaborn
records = []
for year, base in zip(years, base_trade):
    low   = round(base * 0.98, 3)
    high  = round(base * 1.02, 3)
    for scen, val in zip(scenarios, [low, base, high]):
        records.append({"Year": year, "Scenario": scen, "TradeVolume": val})

df = pd.DataFrame.from_records(records)

# --------------------------------------------------------------
# Plot: grouped bar chart (Year on x‑axis, TradeVolume on y, hue=Scenario)
# --------------------------------------------------------------
sns.set_style("whitegrid")
plt.figure(figsize=(14, 8))

# Use a distinct pastel palette different from the original

    x="Year",
    y="TradeVolume",
    hue="Scenario",

base_totals = [
    152800, 103000, 119500, 93600, 57700, 73440,

]

# Gender split – 52 % male, 48 % female (unchanged)
male_counts   = [int(t * 0.52) for t in total_children]
female_counts = [t - m for t, m in zip(total_children, male_counts)]

    "Canada":        [ 72.0,  76.5,  81.0,  93.0],
    "UK":             [ 79.0,  80.5,  82.0,  86.0],
    "France":        [ 68.0,  71.5,  75.0,  84.0],

    "Netherlands":   [ 45.0,  46.5,  48.0,  57.0],
}

# Build a tidy DataFrame

for country, vals in savings_by_country.items():

        records.append({"Year": yr, "Country": country, "Savings": val})
df = pd.DataFrame.from_records(records)

# ---------- Bar Chart ----------
sns.set_style("whitegrid")
palette = sns.color_palette("Set2")  # distinct, aesthetically pleasing palette

import pandas as pd
import seaborn as sns
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt

# --------------------------------------------------------------
# Data: Estimated subsidy amounts (trillion $) for 1995‑2000
# Minor adjustments: added South Korea, slightly tweaked Brazil.
# --------------------------------------------------------------
base_2000 = {
    "Democratic Republic of Congo": 0.25,
    "Kazakhstan": 7.3,
    "Russian Federation": 20.8,
    "South Africa": 4.2,
    "Nigeria": 2.6,
    "Vietnam": 2.2,
    "Brazil": 5.5,                 # adjusted from 5.3
    "India": 4.5,
    "Indonesia": 3.5,
    "Argentina": 3.2,
    "South Korea": 3.0            # new entry
}

years = list(range(1995, 2001))          # 1995‑2000
scale = {year: (year - 1990) / 10 for year in years}   # 0.5, 0.6, …, 1.0

# Build a flat table: one row per (year, country) pair
records = []
for year in years:
    factor = scale[year]
    for country, value_2000 in base_2000.items():
        records.append({
            "Year": year,
            "Country": country,
            "Subsidy": round(value_2000 * factor, 2)   # two‑decimal precision
        })

df = pd.DataFrame(records)

# --------------------------------------------------------------
# Aggregate to total subsidy per country across all years
# --------------------------------------------------------------
total_by_country = (
    df.groupby("Country", as_index=False)["Subsidy"]
      .sum()
      .rename(columns={"Subsidy": "TotalSubsidy"})
)

# --------------------------------------------------------------
# Plotting a bar chart with seaborn
# --------------------------------------------------------------
sns.set_theme(style="whitegrid")
plt.figure(figsize=(12, 6))

barplot = sns.barplot(
    data=total_by_country,
    x="Country",
    y="TotalSubsidy",
    palette="muted"
)

# Add value labels on top of each bar
for p in barplot.patches:
    height = p.get_height()
    barplot.annotate(
        f'{height:.2f}',
        (p.get_x() + p.get_width() / 2., height),
        ha='center',
        va='bottom',
        fontsize=9,
        color='black',
        xytext=(0, 4),
        textcoords='offset points'
    )

plt.title("Total Government Subsidies (1995‑2000) by Country", fontsize=14, pad=15)
plt.xlabel("Country", fontsize=12)
plt.ylabel("Cumulative Subsidy (trillion $)", fontsize=12)
plt.xticks(rotation=45, ha='right')
plt.tight_layout()

# Save the figure as a PNG image
plt.savefig("bar_subsidies.png", dpi=300)
plt.close()

import pandas as pd
import seaborn as sns
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt

# --------------------------------------------------------------
# Updated dataset – unemployment duration (weeks) for young women (15‑24) in Iceland, 2026
# --------------------------------------------------------------
total_young_women = 1600          # total individuals (≈160 k)

# NEET count (≈5.9% of total)
female_neet_count = 95

# Unemployed count (≈6.6% of total)
overall_unemp_count = 105

# Employed count – remainder
employed_count = total_young_women - overall_unemp_count  # 1495 individuals

# --------------------------------------------------------------
# Explicit duration values (weeks) for each subgroup – minor extensions
# --------------------------------------------------------------
# Employed – mostly no unemployment, few short spells
employed_pattern = [0, 0, 0, 1, 2, 3]          # weeks
emp_rep, emp_extra = divmod(employed_count, len(employed_pattern))
employed_durations = employed_pattern * emp_rep + employed_pattern[:emp_extra]

# NEET – short spells of inactivity
neet_pattern = [2, 4, 5, 7, 9]                # weeks
neet_rep, neet_extra = divmod(female_neet_count, len(neet_pattern))
female_neet_durations = neet_pattern * neet_rep + neet_pattern[:neet_extra]

# Unemployed – longer spells of joblessness
unemp_pattern = [12, 14, 16, 18, 20, 22]     # weeks
unemp_rep, unemp_extra = divmod(overall_unemp_count, len(unemp_pattern))
overall_unemp_durations = unemp_pattern * unemp_rep + unemp_pattern[:unemp_extra]

# Assemble tidy DataFrame
df = pd.DataFrame({
    "duration_weeks": (
        employed_durations +
        female_neet_durations +
        overall_unemp_durations
    ),
    "group": (
        ["Employed (active)"] * employed_count +
        ["Female NEET (15‑24)"] * female_neet_count +
        ["Unemployed"] * overall_unemp_count
    )
})

# --------------------------------------------------------------
# Summarise – mean unemployment duration per group
# --------------------------------------------------------------
summary = (
    df.groupby("group", as_index=False)
      .duration_weeks.mean()
      .rename(columns={"duration_weeks": "mean_duration_weeks"})
)

# --------------------------------------------------------------
# Plotting – bar chart of average unemployment duration by group
# --------------------------------------------------------------
sns.set_style("whitegrid")
plt.figure(figsize=(8, 5))

barplot = sns.barplot(
    data=summary,
    x="group",
    y="mean_duration_weeks",
    palette="Set2",          # aesthetic, different from original Pastel
    edgecolor="black"
)

# Add value labels on top of each bar
for container in barplot.containers:
    barplot.bar_label(container, fmt="%.1f", padding=3)

plt.title(
    "Average Unemployment Duration – Young Women (15‑24), Iceland 2026",
    fontsize=14,
    pad=12
)
plt.xlabel("Group", fontsize=12)
plt.ylabel("Mean Duration (weeks)", fontsize=12)
plt.tight_layout()

# Save the figure

import plotly.express as px

regions = [
    'High income',

    'European Union',
    'Europe (all income levels)',
    'North America',
    'South America',
    'Oceania',
    'Africa (all income levels)'          # newly added region
]

categories = [
    'Agricultural Materials',   # renamed
    'Food',
    'Fuel',
    'Manufactured Products',    # renamed
    'Services'
]

# Shares for 2022 (slightly adjusted)
shares_2022 = {
    'Agricultural Materials': [4.3, 11.1, 3.4, 3.3, 4.8, 5.6, 5.3, 5.0],
    'Food':                    [11.5, 49.0, 12.3, 11.8, 14.3, 15.3, 16.4, 16.0],
    'Fuel':                    [8.8, 9.5, 5.8, 5.6, 8.2, 8.4, 9.3, 8.9],
    'Manufactured Products':   [22.5, 4.8, 32.5, 27.3, 24.4, 20.5, 23.5, 23.0],
    'Services':                [8.7, 4.7, 12.7, 10.7, 9.7, 7.7, 7.2, 6.9]
}

# Build a tidy DataFrame suitable for a grouped bar chart
records = []
for cat in categories:
    for region, share in zip(regions, shares_2022[cat]):
        records.append({
            'Region': region,
            'Category': cat,
            'Share_2022': share
        })

df = pd.DataFrame.from_records(records)

# ---- Grouped Bar Chart (2022 shares by region and category) ----
color_palette = px.colors.sequential.Viridis  # pleasing built‑in palette

fig = px.bar(
    df,
    x='Region',
    y='Share_2022',
    color='Category',
    barmode='group',
    text='Share_2022',
    color_discrete_sequence=color_palette,
    title='Export Share by Region & Category (2022)',
    labels={'Share_2022': 'Export Share (%)', 'Region': 'Region'}
)

# Improve layout
fig.update_traces(texttemplate='%{text:.1f}', textposition='outside')
fig.update_layout(
    uniformtext_minsize=8,
    uniformtext_mode='hide',
    xaxis_tickangle=-45,
    margin=dict(l=60, r=20, t=80, b=60),
    legend_title_text='Category',
    legend=dict(title=None, orientation='h', y=-0.2, x=0.5, xanchor='center')
)
# Save static PNG (requires kaleido)

# Variation: ChartType=Bar Chart, Library=plotly
import pandas as pd
import plotly.express as px

# ---- Data (minor adjustments) ----
# Added 2012 for an extended timeline and tweaked values slightly
years = [2007, 2008, 2009, 2010, 2011, 2012]

cost_data = {
    "SSA":           [182, 128, 112,  98,  90,  85],   # Sub‑Saharan Africa (renamed for brevity)
    "Côte d'Ivoire":[136, 133, 138, 134, 130, 128],
    "Jordan":        [ 19,  31,  26,  32,  35,  37]
}

# Convert to tidy DataFrame for Plotly
records = []
for country, values in cost_data.items():
    for yr, val in zip(years, values):
        records.append({"Year": yr, "Country": country, "Cost": val})

df = pd.DataFrame(records)

# ---- Create grouped Bar Chart ----
fig = px.bar(
    df,
    x="Year",
    y="Cost",
    color="Country",
    barmode="group",
    title="Cost of Business Start‑up Procedures by Year",
    labels={"Cost": "% of GNI per capita", "Year": "Year"},
    color_discrete_sequence=px.colors.qualitative.Pastel2,
)

# ---- Layout tweaks for clarity ----
fig.update_layout(
    xaxis=dict(tickmode="linear", tick0=2007, dtick=1),
    yaxis=dict(range=[0, max(df["Cost"]) + 20]),
    legend_title_text="Country",
    legend=dict(x=1.02, y=1, bordercolor="LightGray", borderwidth=1),
    margin=dict(l=60, r=60, t=80, b=60),
)

# ---- Save the figure ----
fig.write_image("bar_chart.png", width=800, height=600, scale=2)
